summary: A streamlined card-game adaptation of Arkwright that keeps the factory-running and market-pricing core but trims the playtime and fiddliness of the original board game. It's still a fairly heavy economic puzzle, just faster and more portable.
praised: captures the economic depth of Arkwright in a shorter format
less table space and setup than the original
criticised: still fairly complex for a "card game"
loses some of the tactile board-game feel of the original
niche appeal to fans of heavy economic games

interaction.kind: economic competition through a shared market
interaction.detail: As in its parent game, each player develops their own factories from their own hand of cards, while a shared market for selling goods and a shared pool of available upgrade cards create indirect competition. Selling into the same market or taking an improvement card before someone else can suppress prices or opportunities for rivals, but no one acts directly on another player's factories.

scoring.how_you_win: Open and upgrade factories with cards over three decades of four rounds each, spending VP as currency; the player with the most valuable block of shares at the end wins.
